gap: No result ChatGPT got ties a lab figure to its own pick: the AlorAir Sentinel HDi65S is certified under the same ENERGY STAR record as the HD55S, which lists 36.33 pints/day at the DOE 65°F/60% RH test (about 66% of the 55-pint AHAM figure ChatGPT quoted), 2.08 L/kWh and 379 kWh/yr. None of the other pump models (HD55P, HD35P, Galaxy 85P, HDi90) are in the ENERGY STAR dataset at all.
standout_why: I checked the two cited rivals, dehumidifierverdict.com and crawlspacedehumidifiers.org/with-pump. Both list the HDi65/HDi65S at 55 pints AHAM only, with no 65°F figure and no ENERGY STAR IEF. dehumidifierverdict says it does no testing. crawlspacedehumidifiers.org gives 73°F figures only for the HDi100/HDi120 and a 65°F figure only for the Seaira NXT85C. crawlspacecosts.com (cited in chat 2) has no DOE or ENERGY STAR data. One uncited result, dryhomelab.com, does give '36.33 pints per day at the portable test condition' for the HD55S. But it calls the HD55S a gravity unit outside its picks and never links that figure to the HDi65S. Bob Vila (uncited) is the only rival with named measurements, and none of them are for a pump model. So rivals hold part of the finding.
decides: The finding confirms the HDi65S as the 55-pint pump pick but resizes it: in a cool crawl space, plan on about 36 pints/day, not 55. It also gives the HDi65S a verifiable efficiency figure (2.08 L/kWh, 379 kWh/yr) that the HD55P, HD35P, Galaxy 85P and HDi90 don't have in ENERGY STAR's data. That favours the HDi65S over the HD55P when running cost matters. Our page leads with the HD55P, so it should say the HD55P has no ENERGY STAR listing.
